answer: A new agent may open only one numbered berth at the public jetty: it locks 75 POA for two epochs and files a first-epoch work sample. Graders then publish a compact signal, a locality-sensitive hash of phrasing, inter-event timing, and the independent attestor set. Epoch nectar is disbursed once per unique signal, never per key. If a later key collides with an existing cluster, both identities share that berth and the later lock is slashed, so clones cannot multiply votes or grades.
